A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CodeLutra research. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support comparison, including content relocated between sections.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, ablations, error analyses, and code-quality assessment experiments, including results in its appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds an MBPP evaluation in Appendix B.4 and Table 9.

M1.justification: The iterative generation, execution-based preference construction, replacement-sampling rule, and combined DPO/SFT objective are retained. Algorithm 1 moves into the main text and is reformatted without changing its procedure.

E1.justification: v3 adds evaluation on MBPP from EvalPlus, extending coverage to general programming problems. Spider, BIRD, and DS-1000 remain, including their existing evaluation scenarios.

E2.justification: The reported comparator sets are retained, including self-debugging and GPT-4 preferences. However, v3's new Table 5 lists StarCoder-15B, while its result tables retain StarCoder-7B/StarCoder2-7B labels. The PDFs do not resolve whether this indicates a comparator change or a documentation error.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes the reported number of sampled responses per question from 16 to 10. Temperature, four one-epoch iterations, preference-pair count, retained dataset splits, and training hyperparameters remain unchanged. This is a reported setting revision, without evidence establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The negative-sample, training-size, ground-truth, and SFT-regularization ablations are retained, alongside the error analyses, qualitative case, and appendix assessment experiments. MBPP adds benchmark coverage rather than a new diagnostic analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v3's new discussion of bootstrapping-like sampling concerns possible future work, not statistical estimation applied to reported results.

E6.justification: Matched existing numerical results and plotted findings are retained. v3 adds Table 9's MBPP accuracies: base model 52.3%, SFT 53.1%, and CodeLutra 55.4%. These are additional benchmark results, not demonstrated performance changes under an existing setting.

T1.justification: v3 adds the standard autoregressive probability factorization as background explanation. Its optimization equations match mathematics already present in v2, including Algorithm 1. No substantive new assumptions, derivations, proofs, or theoretical guarantees are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and first contribution reframe CodeLutra from introducing a novel framework toward exploring existing preference-learning developments for code generation. The performance and data-efficiency claims remain, and the body still claims the first comprehensive study.

C2.justification: v3 adds a mechanism explanation connecting DPO's likelihood decline to proxy rewards and misdirected gradients, and interprets iteration saturation as convergence. Appendix C newly discusses limitations of preference-pair sampling and possible benefits of consistently sampling with replacement.

D1.justification: v3 adds checkpoint identifiers and proprietary-model versions in Appendix A.5, plus task-specific automated verification details in Section 5.1. The StarCoder checkpoint conflicts with result labels. Table 2 also drops v2's statement that DPO was fine-tuned on an SFT model; this omission does not establish a procedural change.

R1.justification: v3 adds the EvalPlus reference and substitutes related-work citations, including REACC and InstructCoder. Much of the apparently expanded Section 2 reproduces v2's extended literature discussion in Appendix A, so the research positioning is largely retained.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution wording, and front matter receive edits, with short background and explanatory additions. The extended literature discussion and pseudocode move into the main text, while the main section sequence and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column formatting to a single-column TMLR layout, substantially reflowing text, figures, tables, and equations. Algorithm 1 gains line numbering, the SQL case moves from appendix Figure 7 to main-text Figure 5, and checkpoint and MBPP tables are added.

improvement.justification: The MBPP comparison modestly broadens empirical support, while checkpoint versions and verification details improve documentation. These gains are limited by sparse MBPP protocol reporting and the new StarCoder checkpoint inconsistency. The central method and existing results remain unchanged, supporting a limited overall improvement.
